title: When life and practice do not match
issueStatement: The line is loved in speech but not yet trusted enough to govern ordinary behavior. The strain is the quiet split between devotion and the next visible act.

pressure.label: Under Pressure
pressure.title: When pressure exposes the gap between image and conduct
pressure.issueStatement: The strain is rising, and what slips first is not language but alignment. Under pressure, the person you present and the person you practice begin separating in visible ways.
pressure.centralInsight: Gurbani measures conduct where pressure would excuse compromise. Practice becomes real when stress does not automatically earn the ego permission to lower the standard it publicly praises.
pressure.practicalReflection: Pressure does not create the gap; it reveals what was only being maintained when conditions were favorable. This is why the moment is useful, even when it is humbling.

repair.centralInsight: Gurbani repairs conduct through truthfulness, not branding. The way back is to stop polishing the claim and start cleaning the action that made the claim ring hollow.
repair.practicalReflection: Repairing conduct often begins in embarrassment, but it becomes fruitful when the embarrassment is used for correction instead of concealment.
